description: My name is bilal, and a student at University of Oslo
summary:
FireSeason turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire data into one consistent record that fire planners can use. Since 2018 the sharper VIIRS sensor reports about four hotspots for every one MODIS sees, so raw counts make fire activity look like it exploded. In Europe raw data suggests 2.15 times more fire in 2019–2025 than in 2001–2017, while counted the same way it fell to 0.62 times. With MODIS near end of life, the record breaks unless the two sensors are harmonized.

We convert VIIRS to MODIS level per 5° tile and calendar month, and test it on years the model never saw, with a typical monthly error of 9–11% for the USA, Europe and California. The web app answers a planner’s questions in plain language: when the fire season is, whether this year is normal, whether it is changing, and where activity is unusual for each place. It covers California, Greece, the USA and Europe, and users can draw any area on a map.
